# bidser

<!-- badges: start -->
[![CRAN status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/bidser)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=bidser)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/bidser/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/bidser/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![pkgdown](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/bidser/actions/workflows/pkgdown.yaml/badge.svg)](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/bidser/)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/bbuchsbaum/bidser/branch/master/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/bbuchsbaum/bidser?branch=master)
<!-- badges: end -->

**bidser** reads a [BIDS](https://bids.neuroimaging.io/) (Brain Imaging Data
Structure) dataset into R and answers the questions that come before any
analysis:

- what is in the dataset, and is anything missing or malformed;
- where the files for a given subject, session, task and run are;
- what the sidecar metadata say, with BIDS inheritance applied;
- which derivative pipelines (fMRIPrep and others) have run, and on what;
- which confound regressors to use, and whether head motion is a problem.

It works on the directory as it sits on disk, with no Python, external
validator or imaging package required.

[Documentation](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/bidser/) ·
[Getting started](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/bidser/articles/quickstart.html) ·
[Derivatives](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/bidser/articles/derivatives.html) ·

## Installation

```r
install.packages("bidser")                    # CRAN release
remotes::install_github("bbuchsbaum/bidser")  # development version
```

## Open a dataset

Point `bids_project()` at the dataset root. `derivatives = "auto"` also
picks up any pipelines under `derivatives/`.

```{r open}
library(bidser)

proj <- bids_project(path, derivatives = "auto")
proj
```

The examples on this page run on a small demonstration dataset: a two-session
working-memory study with 10 subjects, `anat`, `func`, `fmap` and `dwi` data,
and fMRIPrep output. It is written by
[`data-raw/readme-dataset.R`](data-raw/readme-dataset.R) and has a few planted
problems so the checks below have something to find. Any BIDS directory works
the same way, and `get_example_bids_dataset("ds001")` downloads a real one.

## See what is there, and what is not

`plot_bids()` draws one row per subject (grouped by session) and one column
per acquisition (grouped by datatype, task and pipeline). Files that are
present are drawn pale, so the dark marks are the problems. A cross marks a
missing file. A framed fraction marks a run with fewer volumes than its column
usually has, read from the NIfTI header. A ring marks a run without its
`events.tsv`. Every problem is listed under the plot by BIDS file name.

```{r plot-bids, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 7.6}
plot_bids(proj, interactive = FALSE)
```

`plot_bids_tree()` shows the same dataset as a file layout. Every subject is
folded into one `sub-<label>` template, and each file line gives its count and
names whoever is missing.

```{r plot-tree, fig.width = 12.5, fig.height = 7}
plot_bids_tree(proj)
```

For the same checks as data rather than pictures, see `bids_report()`,
`bids_summary()` and `bids_check_compliance()`.

## Find files by entity

`query_files()` filters on any BIDS entity and can return a tibble of parsed
entities instead of paths. Filters are regular expressions by default;
`match_mode = "exact"` and `"glob"` are also available.

```{r query}
query_files(proj, regex = "bold\\.nii\\.gz$", subid = "01", task = "nback",
            scope = "raw", return = "tibble")[, c("subid", "session", "task", "run", "kind")]
```

Convenience wrappers cover the common cases: `func_scans()`, `event_files()`,
`preproc_scans()`, `confound_files()`, `mask_files()`.

## Metadata, volumes and events

`get_metadata()` resolves a file's sidecar with BIDS inheritance, so a
`RepetitionTime` set once in `task-nback_bold.json` at the dataset root
applies to every run:

```{r metadata}
bold <- func_scans(proj, subid = "01", task = "nback", session = "pre", run = "1")
get_metadata(proj, bold)[c("TaskName", "RepetitionTime")]
```

`n_volumes()` reads volume counts from the image headers. Here it shows the
run that stopped early:

```{r volumes}
n_volumes(proj, subid = "07", session = "post", task = "nback", as_tibble = TRUE)[
  , c("subid", "session", "run", "nvols")]
```

`read_events()` returns each run's `events.tsv` nested by subject, session,
task and run:

```{r events}
read_events(proj, subid = "01", session = "pre", task = "nback")
```

## Derivatives

Pipelines under `derivatives/` are discovered from their
`dataset_description.json`, and every query can be scoped to raw data, to
derivatives, or to one pipeline:

```{r derivatives}
derivative_pipelines(proj)[, c("pipeline", "root")]

query_files(proj, regex = "desc-preproc_bold", scope = "derivatives",
            pipeline = "fmriprep", subid = "09", session = "post")
```

Only two preprocessed runs are returned for sub-09 ses-post, where three were
expected. That is the failed run marked in the matrix above.

## Confounds and head motion

`read_confounds()` reads fMRIPrep confound tables, selecting columns by named
sets that adapt to the fMRIPrep version (`confound_set("motion24")`, `"36p"`,
`"acompcor"`, ...) or reducing them with a PCA strategy:

```{r confounds}
read_confounds(proj, subid = "01", session = "pre", cvars = confound_set("motion6"))
```

Keep framewise displacement as a raw column and `plot()` leads with head
motion. Each dot is one run, placed by the share of its volumes above the
threshold (0.5 mm by default):

```{r confound-plot, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6.2}
strategy <- confound_strategy(
  pca_vars = c("global_signal", "csf", "white_matter", "trans_*", "rot_*"),
  raw_vars = "framewise_displacement",
  npcs = 4
)
plot(read_confounds(proj, cvars = strategy), view = "aggregate")
```

`list_confound_sets()` and `list_confound_strategies()` list the built-in
options. Code that used the unexported `bidser:::DEFAULT_CVARS2` should switch
to `confound_set("legacy_default")`, which returns the same 26 columns.

## Testing code without data

`create_mock_bids()` builds an in-memory project from a table of files. It can
optionally write zero-byte stubs (plus event and confound tables) to disk. The
query, event, confound and plotting functions accept it, so analysis code can
be tested without downloading anything:

```{r mock}
mock <- create_mock_bids(
  project_name = "demo",
  participants = c("01", "02"),
  file_structure = data.frame(
    subid = c("01", "02"), datatype = "func", task = "rest", run = "01",
    suffix = "bold.nii.gz", fmriprep = FALSE
  )
)
func_scans(mock)
```
